Pretty disappointed with my grill…not but a couple of months old and I’ve finally had enough medium issues that I’m pretty upset with the way this has been performing. My reason for choosing Traeger was I thought I was paying more for quality and durability, though I’ve found this is incorrect. I’ll also let it be known I’ve never written a one star review, pretty bummed this has to be my first.

I’d like to think I take care of my stuff, and very well too. I regularly clean my grill and replace my drip pans, I keep my pellets store in a dry shed, I cover my grill after every cook, all to protect its longevity…. But this hasn’t proven to help much. 

First is my biggest complaint. Today, for the 4th time my grill has started smoking up in the pellet box, not the grill. I had plenty of pellets, and went outside to check the box multiple times- even making sure they were feeding correctly (because I’ve had this issue before a few times) but when set at 250 after not checking on it for about 30 mins I went out to see my grill at 341 degrees and the pellet box smoking like crazy, while my pork was cool enough to handle. I’ve had this before a few times but today has happened 3 times!! After each time I shut it down, put the meat in the oven, let the grill cool off for an hour at least, put it back on and after about an hour it starts messing up again. Very frustrating.

Second- my grill paint is bubbling/chipping. I’ve seen many other reviews on this. I’ve never had a grease fire, nor have I used max heat other than a handful of times… and I keep my grill covered when not in use, so that’s clearly an issue.

Lastly- just to paint a picture about my current frustrations with the Traeger brand… about 1/3 of my pellet bag is bad. I keep my bags off the floor in my shed and this was a brand new unopened bag that was bad… this is the second time I’ve gotten a bag with bad chips… the last time wasn’t quite as much though- this being a third of my bag at least though proved a much bigger annoyance. 

I have many friends with Traegers with positive experiences, unfortunately mine isn’t great. Just beware I guess… inspect your bags to the best extent and be careful to watch your pellet box. Definitely don’t want that thing catching mid cook. I’ve attached a few pictures, unfortunately didn’t think to snag a pic of the box smoking.

If the temperature is correct for the setting, then the smoke should be as expected. Longer cooks at lower temps will produce more smoke into the food.

I can only hope that i will have success as a BBQ repair man and then experience all of the same joy that others have written about.
